definitions.explanation: The act or means of keeping something under control — an emotion, a rise in prices, or one's authority over others.

definitions.gloss: closer; relief pitcher who finishes the game (baseball)
definitions.explanation: The relief pitcher brought in to protect a lead and record the final outs, typically in the last inning.

examples.japanese: {感情|かんじょう}の{抑|おさ}えがきかない。
examples.english: I can't keep my emotions in check.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{若手|わかて}への{抑|おさ}えが{利|き}く。
examples.english: He commands the respect of the younger staff.

examples.japanese: {物価|ぶっか}{上昇|じょうしょう}の{抑|おさ}えとして{対策|たいさく}を{取|と}った。
examples.english: They took measures as a check on rising prices.

examples.japanese: あのチームの{抑|おさ}えは{頼|たよ}りになる。
{九回|きゅうかい}に{抑|おさ}えが{登板|とうばん}した。
examples.english: The closer took the mound in the ninth inning.

examples.japanese: {抑|おさ}えの{投手|とうしゅ}が{最後|さいご}の{打者|だしゃ}を{三振|さんしん}に{仕留|しと}めた。
examples.english: The closing pitcher struck out the final batter.

notes:
The noun form of {抑|おさ}える (to hold down, to restrain). The baseball 'closer' sense pictures the pitcher who holds the opponent down at the end of the game.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {抑|おさ}えが{利|き}く: to have control or authority (over people)
- {抑|おさ}えがきかない: to be unable to keep something in check
- {抑|おさ}えの{投手|とうしゅ}: closing pitcher

SIMILAR WORDS:
- クローザー: closer — the loanword for the same baseball role
- {中継|なかつ}ぎ: middle reliever — pitches earlier, before the closer
